description: This course covers the fundamentals of digital imaging processing, including image acquisition, preprocessing, enhancement, restoration, segmentation, and feature extraction. Topics include image sampling and quantization; JPEG and MPEG compression standards; edge detection using Sobel and Canny operators; histogram equalization; image filtering techniques such as convolution and median filtering; morphological operations like erosion and dilation; and advanced topics such as image registration, object recognition using convolutional neural networks, and image compression with wavelet transforms. The course also explores image databases, color models (RGB, CMYK, HSV), and image storage formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF).

clos.text: Define image sampling and quantization techniques and their impact on image quality and resolution.
Describe the principles and applications of JPEG and MPEG compression standards in digital imaging.
Explain the operation of edge detection algorithms such as Sobel and Canny operators in image processing pipelines.
Apply image filtering techniques including convolution and median filtering to enhance and restore images.
Implement image segmentation methods using thresholding, region growing, and edge-based approaches in a programming environment.
Analyze the effectiveness of morphological operations in noise reduction and shape analysis.
Design a system for image registration that aligns multi-spectral images using feature matching techniques.
Evaluate the performance of convolutional neural networks in object recognition tasks within digital imaging applications.
Construct an image compression algorithm using wavelet transforms and compare its efficiency with JPEG standards.
Design and implement an image database system that supports efficient retrieval and management of digital images.
Evaluate the impact of color models (RGB, CMYK, HSV) on image processing and display technologies.
Construct image storage formats (PNG, JPEG, TIFF) with specific compression and quality parameters.
Analyze the trade-offs between image resolution, file size, and compression quality in different applications.
Design a digital imaging application that integrates image processing, compression, and storage functionalities.
Evaluate the ethical and security implications of digital image processing in modern applications.
